Subject: Trouble logging into supplier portal after invite

Hi Ben,

We completed the onboarding steps for Coupa yesterday and the procurement team is stuck on the final login step. When users click the "Accept & Log in" button they get a modal that says 'Session stale — please retry'. The OTP appears to be generated but the portal rejects it with a timestamp mismatch error.

We've tried: Chrome (Windows 11) and Safari (macOS Ventura), clearing cookies, and different networks — still failing. Attached is a screenshot of the modal and a short excerpt from our auth server logs (ignite_server_auth.log).

Can you help? This is blocking our first PO for next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Amit Patel
Procurement Manager
IgniteWorks

Thanks for the detail, Amit — sorry you're hitting this.

Quick summary of what I need from you to escalate to infra:
- Full server auth log for the attempted login (not just the excerpt)
- Exact timestamp (including TZ) when you clicked Accept for one of the failed attempts
- Browser console capture if possible

I've opened a support incident INC-97421 and looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Rachel (security onboarding). Marissa — can you validate whether our Coupa invite TTL recently changed in the last deploy? Rachel — could the token validation be rejecting requests with Accept-Language or cookie attributes set differently?

Short term workaround suggestion: if users open the invite link in an incognito/private window that skips some persisted cookies, does the button move forward? If that works, it's probably a cookie partition/expiry issue. Please try and tell me results so we can decide whether an immediate TTL bump is acceptable before the deploy.

I'll update INC-97421 with any logs you send.

Best,

Hi Amit — looping in the steps we've seen work in the past and an internal checklist so we can triage quickly. Quoting Ben below for context.

On Fri, Nov 9, 2028 at 10:02 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the detail, Amit — sorry you're hitting this.
> 
> Quick summary of what I need from you to escalate to infra: ...

What we are checking on our side (internal):
- Token TTL and server clock skew: verify server NTP sync and token issued_at vs server time.
- Cookie scope/partition: some enterprise endpoints append SameSite/Partition attrs that cause old cookies to be treated as stale.
- OTP validator: ensure the OTP check uses UTC timestamp and allows a +/- 2 minute window.

Amit — can you confirm the OS time on the user's machine(s)? We had one case where a handheld scanning device on the account had its clock set in a different year and that caused a similar error. Also, please try an incognito window (Ben's suggestion) and a private browser profile — if that succeeds we can create an immediate mitigative plan: 1) invalidate server-side session cookie on invite endpoints, 2) increase accept-window for OTP for a short period, 3) notify inactive sessions to remove old cookies.

If you can paste a single attempt timestamp (e.g., 2028-11-09T15:14:04Z) and the full auth log file, we'll add it to INC-97421 and push to on-call.

Timeline: we'll triage on Monday 2028-11-12 09:00 PST and aim for a short-term config change same day if we can reproduce.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks — attaching the full auth log and the precise timestamp from the failed attempt. We tried incognito and it failed there too, so likely not a browser cookie cache. The device clock looked correct.

Excerpt of the important line from ignite_server_auth.log:
[2028-11-09T15:14:04Z] AUTH_FAIL token_timestamp=2028-11-09T15:12:59Z accepted_window_start=2028-11-09T15:13:00Z reason=issued_before_window

If that log helps, it looks like our token is being interpreted as 1 second earlier than the allowed window — sounds like a rounding/truncation issue on the service that produces the OTP.
